https://med.emory.edu/education/multicultural-med-student-affairs/index.html

The School of Medicine’s Office of Multicultural Affairs (OMA) supports our mission to diversify the medical field. From pre-application activities to celebrating graduates and working with alumni and residents as mentors, OMA supports individuals and groups like Emory’s Student National Medical Association (SNMA), Latino Medical Student Association (LMSA), Medical Pride Alliance (LGBTQ+), and Asian Pacific American Student Assn (APAMSA) to stimulate an active, healthy and diverse community. The Office of Multicultural Affairs also provides support and resources to students from under-represented backgrounds, for example: the EPiC program, a 3-year mentoring relationship with local under-served HS students; the EmPREP webinar series for undergrads, and HealthPREP an 8-week residential program to prepare college students and recent graduates for entry into health-related graduate and professional schools.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Any Leave of Absence for health, personal, or family reasons, or for special academic study, must be approved by the Executive Associate Dean of Medical Education and Student Affairs. If the leave of absence extends beyond one year, the student must apply for readmission, unless a longer period for special study is approved by the Dean.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Medical students are strongly encouraged to explore and enjoy their interests outside of the classroom. Every year new student organizations are created to respond to the talents and interests of the current student body, including athletics, camping, hiking, dance, music, art, volunteerism, activism, business, and ethics, as well as medical and surgical interests. Intramural sports are popular throughout the year and offer inter-class competition, as well as events with other graduate students on campus.  Medical students also gather as individual classes and as an entire student body for annual events such as the Big Sib/Little Sib Dinner, Halloween Ball, Thanksgiving Potluck and Doctoberfest Chili Cook-off  (the annual inter-society Field Day competition).
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Emory School of Medicine is located on the main university campus, situated on 631 acres in the historic neighborhood of Druid Hills, 6 miles from downtown Atlanta. Emory is positioned along the Clifton Corridor, which includes the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Rollins School of Public Health, Wesley Woods Geriatric Center, and Emory University Hospital and Clinics. Additional clinical facilities are located on the main campus and at numerous sites around the Atlanta metro area.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Most students live in close proximity to the main campus. Nearby off-campus rental properties are plentiful and affordable. Two graduate housing facilities, Campus Crossings at Briarcliff and The Ridge are nearby and available to medical students. A Housing Weekend, hosted by current medical students, is held each year in June to assist incoming students in their housing/roommate search.

https://www.med.emory.edu/about/diversity/index.html

The Emory Medical Alliance (EMA) student organization provides support and community for classmates who identify as LGBTQ+.   EMA is dedicated not only to creating a visible community within the medical school, but also to educating all medical students to best serve the LGBTQ+ patient population.  Members of EMA frequently work with the administration to improve LGBTQ+ visibility in the  curriculum and around the school. An LGBTQ Healthcare Week is hosted by EMA and provides education, mentorship, and service opportunities for medical students. Numerous student organizations across the University support LGBTQ+ students and provide networking and support for medical students.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Emory University offers a wide variety of wellness programs to all students; additionally, the School of Medicine has specific programs and dedicated faculty and staff who specifically attend to health science students. The Center for Holistic Student Success (CHSS) at Emory School of Medicine strives to improve access to academic support resources, improve access to mental health resources, and promote trust and sense of belonging within the School of Medicine.
Academic success resources include:  1:1 academic coaching and tutoring opportunities; USMLE preparation resources and classes to improve study strategies.  
Mental health resources include access to:  psychiatric and psychological professionals who offer individual confidential sessions; group sessions for students to discuss personal and professional struggles; cognitively-based compassion courses and other mindfulness training and access to confidential substance abuse counseling.
The School of Medicine very much values individual spiritual growth and development.  In our community, there are a wide variety of chaplains, pastoral counselors, and other religious professionals and/or spiritual services representing many faiths and viewpoints.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The School of Medicine hopes to cultivate a culture that esteems in-person mutually-respectful learning and teaching of humane medicine.  Learners and practitioners are privileged to work with and for patients and their families; the most important goal for all students, faculty, staff, and colleagues is the compassionate relief of suffering.
Emory's MD program is designed to maximize in-person learning in a wide variety of in-patient, out-patient, and community practice environments.  Clinical training begins the first week of the M1 year and continues throughout the curriculum.  Medical students experience a range of specialties and subspecialties in 14+ disciplines prior to choosing residency.  
Emory scientists are renowned for basic and translational research; external annual funding currently exceeds $1 billion.  During the M4 year, students participate in a 5-month research phase joining clinical or basic science research teams.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional attire is required for all clinical training and assessments, as well as all in-class patient presentations.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Medical students receive close mentoring, guidance, and tutoring from their Society and Small Group Leaders.  Additional resources are also available through the Center for Holistic Student Success.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Beginning with the first month of classes, students will have in-class patient presentations throughout the Foundations Phase. The Outpatient Clinical Experience begins in November of the first year.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Lecture, small group, and clinical training throughout all 4 years.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Core clerkships begin halfway through the second year and continue for 12 months.  Senior rotations are scheduled throughout the remainder of the third and fourth years.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Students must attend all lectures when a patient is present.  Other lectures may be required at the discretion of the course directors.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The MD curriculum features a hybrid of lectures, small groups, and enhanced clinical exposure throughout the first 18 months of training, including year-long placements in an outpatient clinic and a community center.  The entire curriculum is now pass/fail.  Students begin 12 months of clinical rotations midway through the second year, followed by a 5-month Research phase which allows time for clinical or bench research, an international experience, or other academic inquiry. The fourth year is highlighted by a Capstone experience which helps further prepare students for entering residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Clinical experiences in primary care are included throughout the curriculum. Each first year medical student is assigned to work in a primary care practice for 12 months (one afternoon, every other week). This Outpatient Experience develops the student's clinical exam skills and gives early emphasis to the important role of the primary care physician. During the second-to-third year, students are required to complete rotations in Adult and Pediatric Primary Care at multiple sites around the Atlanta metro area.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students have the option to extend their 5-month research phase up to an additional 12 months. Alternately, students can apply to dual degree programs such as the MD/MSCR (Masters of Science in Clinical Research) or MD/PhD, for a more extensive research experience.  Students may also be granted leave to participate in a research fellowship, degree program, or externship at another institution.  Approximately 25-30% of each class chooses to spend an extra year (or more) to complete one of these programs.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Emory School of Medicine operates on a 12-month, year-round, academic year.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: First-year students are assigned to community-based sites to engage with members and to propose a program or project that is expected to improve the social and health outcomes for that community.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A five-month research phase during the 4th year provides Emory medical students with the opportunity to conduct a hypothesis-driven research project while working closely with a faculty mentor.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Emory University Hospitals and Clinics, Grady Memorial Hospital, Children's Healthcare of Atlanta, Atlanta VA Medical Center, and Wesley Woods Geriatric Hospital.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: The entire curriculum (pre-clinical and clinical) is now Pass/Fail. Emory believes that a pass/fail grading system encourages life-long learning, mitigates inequities, and promotes student well-being.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The Emory University School of Medicine was founded in 1915, resulting from several reorganizations dating from 1854 when the Atlanta Medical College was founded. Student clinical experiences take place in numerous teaching hospitals, which provide more than 3,000 beds and large outpatient clinics. The University has close ties with Grady Memorial Hospital, the Atlanta VA Medical Center, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Carter Center of Emory University, and other local institutions.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
We are committed to recruiting and developing a class of students with the potential to become innovative leaders in biomedical science, public health, medical education, and clinical care. We foster a culture that integrates leading-edge basic, translational, and clinical research to further the ability to deliver quality health care, predict illness, treat the sick, and promote the health of our patients and our communities.  Our mission objectives are as follows:
-Provide outstanding educational programs for medical and graduate students and healthcare professionals
-Develop outstanding lifelong learners who will provide the highest quality compassionate care and will serve the needs of their communities in the best traditions of our profession
-Conduct innovative and collaborative research and integrate this knowledge into the practice of medicine
-Advance the early detection, treatment, and prevention of disease
-Ensure the highest ethical and professional standards in all endeavors

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Ultimately, the decision about which letters to submit is yours.  We require two letters from professors, or others who can speak to your abilities in the "hard sciences":  biology, chemistry/organic chemistry, and physical (earth) science (neither engineering nor psychology are considered the “hard sciences”).  Biomedical course professors are acceptable, but we definitely recommend that the second letter be from a professor in one of the hard sciences.  

We strongly suggest you submit two letters from the professors who taught you in the sciences in your undergraduate or post-bacc. education or from someone familiar with your research and knowledge in the sciences.  If you are unable to submit letters from two science professors, you may substitute letters from other educators, advisors, or employers, but keep in mind that Emory is an extremely competitive school.  The Admissions Committee will look for applicants who demonstrate a sound knowledge in the sciences.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: Applicants will need to submit a Pre-Health or Pre-Medical Committee letter, a packet of letters from a letter-writing or career service, or three letters from individual letter-writers (two of which should be from science professionals).  Letters must be submitted via the AMCAS Letters Service.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Applicants who are selected for an interview will be notified by email. (Please be sure to keep your email address up to date in AMCAS.)  The Interview Season will begin in September and end in February.
The Interview Day will include a welcome session with the Dean and Associate Director of Admissions, two interviews (a group interview and a one-on-one interview), and the opportunity to speak with current medical students, faculty and Admissions staff. A meeting with a current Emory medical student is  available upon request.  Applicants to the MD/MPH and MD/MA in Bioethics Programs will also meet with a representative of the Rollins School of Public Health or the Emory Center for Ethics, respectively, on their Interview Day.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: All 2026-27 interviews will be conducted remotely on the Zoom platform.  All interview days will include both a Group Interview and a One-on-One interview.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All 2026 - 27 interview days will be conducted remotely on the Zoom platform.

medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Out-of-state applicants are eligible for admission.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Canadian applicants are eligible for admission.  Canadian applicants are considered "International" applicants and are not eligible for need-based financial aid.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: International applicants are eligible for admission.  If your undergrad degree is from abroad, all science requirements must be completed at a regionally accredited institution in the US or Canada.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Emory welcomes applications from all persons, regardless of citizenship or visa status.  Citizenship is not used to determine selection for an interview or for acceptance.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
We will accept MCAT scores as far back as 4 years prior to matriculation.  So, for Fall 2027 matriculants, we will accept MCAT scores from 2023 through October 2026.  But we strongly recommend that you take the exam as early as possible. It is important to both apply early and to know your MCAT scores when you submit your AMCAS application. This will allow you to apply to schools where your application will be competitive.  Please also remember that you must meet our MCAT prescreening criteria of 502 total AND at least a 124 in each of the four subtests in order to receive an invitation to complete the Emory Supplemental Application.

Applicants are expected to follow the AAMC Application and Acceptance Protocols for Applicants.  Accepted applicants may hold only one acceptance to medical school after April 30.  By June 1st, accepted applicants must accept "Plan to Enroll" and by July 20, accepted applicants must select "Commit to Enroll" for Emory School of Medicine in the AMCAS Choose Your Medical School (CYMS) Tool.

Additionally, accepted applicants must comply with all terms of their acceptance and must submit all required information, forms, and training required prior to beginning medical school in August.  This includes a background check, drug screening and completion of all training, immunization and vaccination requirements.  Full details will be shared with accepted applicants.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
If you've taken multiple MCAT's, the Admissions Committee will see all your test scores individually.  Test scores are not averaged.  The Committee will see all your scores for each subtest for each exam taken.

Emory will consider your first 3 MCAT's only, regardless of how long ago any of the exams were taken.  Once you've taken the MCAT 3 times, subsequent test scores won't be considered for either prescreening purposes or by the  Committee.  If you have more than 3 MCAT scores, we will notify you that this exceeds our maximum.  If your scores are competitive with our mean, we'll provide an opportunity to request an exception.  To be eligible, your latest  scores should be at – or above – our mean (between 128 & 130 on each subtest, and a 515 total score).  This would be especially appropriate if there are significant changes in your personal and professional circumstances that have affected not only your latest MCAT scores, but your commitment to your medical education, as well.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo:
For the 2026- 27 Application Cycle, Emory will prescreen applicants for minimum MCAT scores.

Emory will prescreen all applicants for a minimum MCAT score of 502 with at least a 124 in each of the four subtests. Applicants with an MCAT total score of less than 502, or a subtest score of less than 124 on any of the four MCAT subtests will not receive an invitation to complete an Emory Supplemental Application.

If an applicant has more than one MCAT score, the latest score will be used to determine eligibility.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: There is no minimum GPA considered.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA considered.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: There is no minimum number of credit hours.  An applicant’s entire file, including all postbacc or graduate coursework will be reviewed holistically.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Emory School of Medicine will accept coursework completed at a community college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Although Emory does not accept Letters of Intent or Expressions of Interest, you may update your application by logging into the Supplemental Portal and selecting the “Application Update” tab.  Please note that only text updates will be accepted.  The application does not have functionality for uploading attachments of any kind.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: A full listing of all technical standards is shared with applicants in advance of their Interview Day.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The financial aid status of an applicant is not a determining factor in the admissions process.  Those who establish documented financial need are eligible to receive funding in the form of scholarships and loans.  Parental financial information is necessary to determine institutional need-based funding.

Each year, Emory awards 6 entering students the merit-based Woodruff Fellowship, which provides full tuition and a small stipend for all four years of medical school.  All accepted applicants (with or without DACA status and regardless of citizenship) are eligible for the same merit-based scholarships available to domestic students.  No separate application for the Woodruff Fellowship is required.  All accepted applicants are automatically considered for this very prestigious award.

International students are expected to secure their own funding for tuition and living expenses.  International students are not eligible for federal student loans, however those with high financial need may be awarded some institutional aid depending on the availability of funds.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: A student is not allowed to register for a subsequent semester until all past due financial obligations are paid. When a student account has an overdue balance, an indicator is placed on the account. In addition to preventing future registration, this indicator may also deny access to University services. The University may not furnish transcripts or diplomas if a student is delinquent in paying student account or loan obligations.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Applicants may apply directly to the MD/MPH, MD/MA in Bioethics and MD/PhD programs on the Emory Supplemental Application.  Students may also choose to apply to the MD/MPH and MD/MA in Bioethics programs anytime up until December of the third year of medical school.  Students may also decide to apply to the MD/PhD program, but an application and interview must be completed by the end the first year.  Medical students may also complete an MS in Clinical Research (MSCR), an MBA, or a Master of Legal Studies (MLS) at Emory, but a separate application is required and students are urged to apply or state their interest in these programs early in their MD curriculum to allow for maximum scheduling options.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Applicants must meet the following course requirements:

(a)  Eight semester hours of Biology with lab, eight semester hours of Inorganic (General) Chemistry with lab; eight semester hours of Organic Chemistry with lab and eight semester hours of Physical Science (Physics, Geology or Astronomy) with lab.  If you do not meet the minimum science requirements, you'll be given an opportunity in the Supplemental Application to explain why.  Exceptions are made.  They are rare, but they are made for individuals with very high grades in the sciences, or high MCAT scores, or strong LOR's from those who can speak to your abilities in the hard sciences, published research, etc. 

(b)  Six semester hours (two classes) of English and

(c)   Eighteen semester hours (six classes) of Humanities/Social Sciences.  For a complete list of accepted Humanities/Social Sciences coursework, please see below and/or the FAQ's on our website:  https://med.emory.edu/education/programs/md/admissions/index.html
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no expiration date for any coursework - prerequisite or otherwise.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: We seek a class of students who will ultimately become humane, competent physicians in our world's communities. All applicants must: (a) present a very high level of scholarship and leadership; (b) demonstrate a strong motivation to practice medicine; (c) have experience in a clinical setting; (d) take the MCAT within four years of the matriculating year and meet our MCAT prescreening criteria; (e) complete the AMCAS application and the Emory Supplemental Application; (f) submit the required letter(s) of recommendation; and, (g) appear for a personal interview, if invited. Students from foreign schools must complete all science course requirements at a regionally accredited institution in the U.S. or a similarly-accredited institution in Canada. Emory University does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, ethnic or national origin, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, veteran status, or any factor prohibited by law.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Applicants should have experience in a clinical setting, directly observing the patient-physician relationship.  The Emory School of Medicine does not specifically require shadowing, although the Admissions Committee will look for you to speak thoughtfully about your experience(s) in the clinical setting on both your application and, potentially, on your interview day.
